answer: An agent economy can split a fixed reward among every agent that submits identical work, so a single agent cataloguing a willow grove earns the full 10 dollars while each of 100 clones doing the same job earns only 10 cents. Each clone still costs about 1 dollar to run, so running 100 clones costs 100 dollars for a shared 10 dollar reward, a loss of about 90 dollars on that job, whether the work is a lantern inspection report or a juniper planting summary. It is like splitting one pie among a hundred guests: each slice gets thinner as more guests arrive.
